title: Agents - generate titles for untitled external sessions
body:
External sessions whose provider surfaces them without a title showed up unnamed in the sessions list. This generates one from the user's first prompt, reusing the existing rename infrastructure.

### Deferred work

Rather than an ad-hoc timer, `AgentService` gets a single lane for maintenance that is fine to run late:

- `markStartupComplete()` is the explicit signal, called by the process mains — `agentHostMain` once every ingress is wired, `agentHostServerMain` when it reports `READY`.
- Work queued through `_runWhenStartupSettled(name, work)` runs once that signal **and** the first served session listing have both happened, so background work never competes with startup. Jobs are serialized, failures are logged per job, and a disposal guard keeps work off a torn-down service.
- The stale external-session prune moves onto the same lane, replacing its 60s timer. The service now owns no ambient timer, which also keeps tests deterministic — they opt in via `markStartupComplete()`.

### Titling external sessions

- Discovery and legacy migration queue newly registered external sessions that carry no provider title.
- The job keeps the **2 most recently updated** candidates, reads the first user prompt from the default chat, and hands it to `AgentHostSessionTitleController.generateExternalSessionTitle` — the same utility-model prompt, cleaning, persistence and cancellation used for first-message titling.
- A session that already carries a persisted title is left alone, and a rename during generation cancels it.
- These sessions are surfaced but not live, so `AgentHostStateManager.updateSurfacedSessionTitle` pushes the title onto the surfaced summary and clients update in place; live sessions still go through the reducer.

### Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client` clean.
- 665 tests pass across the `agentService`, `agentHostSessionTitleController`, `agentHostStateManager` and `agentSideEffects` suites, including four new tests: deferred titling of the 2 most recent candidates, surfaced-summary retitling, not clobbering a concurrent rename, and keeping an existing persisted title.
- The 7 `sessionPermissions` failures visible in a wider run reproduce on a clean checkout of this branch, so they are pre-existing and unrelated.

### Summary Clicking a chat request row while it is shown in sticky scroll throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'id')` in the `onDidClickRequest` handler of `ChatWidget`. The handler validates `item.currentElement`, then calls `this.listWidget.reveal(...)`, which synchronously recycles the sticky-row template and sets `templateData.currentElement = undefined`. The next line re-reads `item.currentElement.id` on the now-cleared template and crashes. Impact: 106 affected users on the target insider build across Windows/Mac/Linux. Fixes microsoft/vscode\#331980 Recommended reviewer: `@justschen` ### Culprit Commit | Field | Value | |-------|-------| | Commit | [`fdf686d3`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/fdf686d3ea1ff5c371174e886962aa0a2ac4cdad) | | Author | `@justschen` | | PR | #296433 | | Message | sticky scroll in chat (#296433) | | Why | This commit introduced the sticky-scroll click handling block in `chatWidget.ts` (`onDidClickRequest`). It reads `item.currentElement` twice — once inside the `isRequestVM(...)` guard and again after `this.listWidget.reveal(...)`. `reveal()` re-renders the sticky row, and `renderChatTreeItem` → `clearRenderedParts` sets `templateData.currentElement = undefined`, so the second read dereferences `undefined`. | ### Code Flow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant User as User participant Renderer as chatListRenderer participant Handler as ChatWidget.onDidClickRequest participant List as ChatListWidget.reveal User->>Renderer: click sticky request row Renderer->>Handler: _onDidClickRequest.fire(templateData) Note over Handler: guard passes:
isRequestVM(item.currentElement) === true Handler->>List: reveal(item.currentElement, 0) Note over List: ⚠️ Root cause:
re-render recycles sticky template,
clearRenderedParts sets
currentElement = undefined Handler->>Handler: read item.currentElement.id Note over Handler: 💥 TypeError:
Cannot read properties of
undefined (reading 'id') ``` ### Affected Files | File | Role | Evidence | |------|------|----------| | `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/chatWidget.ts` | crash site + fix | L2001 (from stack): `getTemplateDataForRequestId(item.currentElement.id)` read after `reveal()` | | `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/chatListRenderer.ts` | producer | L1208: `templateData.currentElement = undefined` in `clearRenderedParts`, reached via `reveal()` → `renderChatTreeItem` (L1214-1222) | ### Repro Steps 1. Enable chat sticky scroll and inline/edit request features (default on insiders). 2. Open a chat session with enough requests that an earlier request scrolls into the sticky-scroll header. 3. Click the request row while it is displayed in the sticky-scroll header. 4. The synchronous `reveal()` recycles the sticky template and clears its `currentElement`, so the subsequent `.id` read throws. This is timing-sensitive: it only reproduces when the clicked row is the sticky-scroll row whose template is recycled during `reveal()`. ### How the Fix Works **Chosen approach** (`chatWidget.ts`): Capture the view model into a local `const clickedElement = item.currentElement` at the top of the handler, before `reveal()` runs, and use `clickedElement` for both the `isRequestVM` guard and the `.id` read. title: agentHost: measure time to first edit
body:
## Why

Agent Host needs an authoritative time-to-first-edit measurement for Copilot SDK turns. Joining the existing SDK usage, failure, cancellation, and assistant-message events cannot reproduce the historical metric because those signals have different lifecycle boundaries and incomplete correlation.

Uses the atomic per-attempt lifecycle event from github/copilot-agent-runtime#16674, which is present in the runtime now bundled on main.

## What

Qualifying `agentHost.turnCompleted` events now include cumulative provider-dispatch time through the first accepted response requesting a built-in file edit. For example:

```json
{
  "timeToFirstEdit": 700,
  "timeToFirstEditClassifierVersion": 1
}
```

Errors, cancellations, post-request rejections, and accepted non-edit responses contribute to the prefix. Root and subagent turns are tracked independently. Turns without a qualifying edit leave both fields absent rather than reporting zero. Shell-based file writes are outside the built-in edit classifier.

Steering turns receive their own completion telemetry and edit timing, including when steering is promoted before the next SDK assistant turn starts. Resumed subagents begin tracking at turn start so their initial failed or rejected attempts contribute too.

## How

The session wrapper validates the raw `model.call_finished` stream into a precise local type because the pinned SDK TypeScript union predates the event. Agent Host maps these events to their owning turns, rejecting duplicates and stale correlation IDs. Provider-promoted steering turns are registered with the telemetry tracker, and their user-message interaction ID is bound immediately.

## Manual validation

Exercised normal turns and steering in an isolated Windows Code OSS Agents window, verifying actual SDK tool names, file contents, and `agentHost.turnCompleted` telemetry rather than relying on UI edit labels.

| Scenario | Actual edit tool | Model | `timeToFirstEdit` | Classifier version | Model calls |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Normal turn (September 9) | `apply_patch` | GPT-5.6 Luna | 7123 ms | 1 | 3 |
| Steering (September 9, 04f75c749f83) | `apply_patch` | GPT-5.6 Luna | 2353 ms | 1 | 5 |
| New-file creation (September 10, 068bf7353a6) | `create` | MAI-Code-1.1-Flash | 3958 ms | 1 | 3 |
| Existing-file replacement (September 10, 068bf7353a6) | `edit` | MAI-Code-1.1-Flash | 1679 ms | 1 | 2 |

The normal `apply_patch` run recorded successful dispatch durations of 4825, 2298, and 1423 ms, with the edit requested by the second call: the metric correctly reported 4825 + 2298, not wall-clock time or the final-response duration. The steering probe submitted a message during an active PowerShell wait. The specific model-call-before-next-assistant-turn-start ordering is covered by a regression test, not forced by the live scenario.

The September 10 probes used runtime 1.0.84-3 and `--log trace` without source instrumentation. Host telemetry is now in `agentHostTelemetry.log`. Both `create` and `edit` produced the exact requested contents and populated timing fields.

Also requested `str_replace_editor` explicitly with MAI-Code-1.1-Flash and Claude Sonnet 5. Neither exposed that tool; the runtime tool-definition trace for Claude confirmed `create` and `edit`, but no `str_replace_editor`. Both probes left the target unchanged and correctly omitted both edit-timing fields. This is an availability/negative-path check, **not** live coverage of a `str_replace_editor` edit.

### Scope and limitations

- These probes explicitly request named tools and do not measure natural tool-selection frequency or recall over all file changes. An earlier unconstrained request selected PowerShell `Set-Content`; that write was skipped before redirecting to a built-in edit tool. Shell writes are outside this classifier.
- Normal-turn details remain in the investigation transcript; its temporary raw logs were cleaned up. Sanitized telemetry evidence and screenshots were retained for the final steering run and the September 10 tool probes.

title: sessions: gate opening a session on workspace trust
body:
## What

Opening a session from the Agents Window sessions list now checks workspace trust:

- **Refuse-to-open**: clicking a session (or Alt-click "open to the side") whose folder is not trusted surfaces VS Code's **standard workspace-trust dialog**. If the user declines, the session does **not** open — the currently-open session stays active, or the empty new-session slot remains if none was open. If the user grants trust, the session opens (and trust is remembered).
- **Worktrees are auto-trusted**: an isolated git worktree that VS Code created off an already-trusted repository is trusted automatically, so worktree sessions open without an extra prompt. Trust is only granted for a genuine worktree cut from a trusted base, so trust never flows from an untrusted repo into its worktree.
- **No silent trust / no Restricted Mode surprises**: the previous behavior silently force-trusted a session's folder on open. That is removed. The workspace folder is never mounted while untrusted, so the window can't silently drop into Restricted Mode — this also keeps paths that bypass the open gate (startup restore, deep links) safe.

## Why

Previously, opening a session in the Agents Window silently trusted its folder, bypassing the workspace-trust prompt the user would otherwise see. This gates the act of opening on trust, using the standard trust UX, while preserving the seamless worktree flow.

## How it works

- `ISessionsService.canOpenSession(session)` is the gate: it fast-passes when the session doesn't require trust or its mounted folder (`folders[0]`) is already trusted, otherwise it raises the standard `requestResourcesTrust` dialog and returns the user's choice.
- The gate runs in the sessions list's `onDidOpen`, before mark-read / activation / mount — so a refused open has no side effects and covers both list-click and Alt-click. Running from this imperative path (not the reactive mount) means the prompt fires once and cannot loop.
- `WorkspaceFolderManagementContribution` now auto-trusts a worktree only when its base repo is trusted, and never mounts an untrusted folder (backstop).

## Scope / follow-ups

- In scope: list click + Alt-click "open to the side".
- Deferred: explicitly gating deep links and startup restore (the mount backstop already keeps them Restricted-safe), and gating the automations/blocked flat-lists.

## Tests

- New `workspaceFolderManagement.test.ts` (7 cases): worktree auto-trust off a trusted base, no auto-trust off an untrusted base, untrusted folder not mounted + never silently granted, switch-to-untrusted unmounts, no-folder, non-trust sessions mount.
- Existing sessions-list / rename / context-menu suites pass.
- `tsc`, ESLint, and `valid-layers-check` clean.

body:
Title: Alt-Tab away and back leaves a tab's Close button stuck showing "Close Other Editors"

## Description

The new Alt+click "Close Others" tab action (#328975, #331435, #331772) can end up
visually stuck in its swapped state after switching to another application and back
with Alt-Tab, even though Alt is no longer held. Clicking the tab's close button then
closes every other tab in the group instead of the one clicked - without the user
having consciously pressed Alt at all in that moment.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open at least two editor tabs in the same group.
2. Hover the mouse over one tab's close button (or leave the mouse resting over a tab
   after closing/opening something there).
3. Press and hold **Alt**, then press **Tab** to switch to another application (a
   browser, another editor, etc.) - a normal OS-level Alt-Tab, releasing Alt only once
   focus has already moved to the other application.
4. Work in the other application for a moment, then switch focus back to VS Code
   (click on the window, or Alt-Tab back) **without moving the mouse away from the tab
   bar**.
5. Click the close "x" on the tab that still has focus/hover from step 2.

## Expected

The tab closes normally, since Alt is not being held at the moment of the click.

## Actual

The tab's close icon is still showing (or reverts to showing) "Close Other Editors",
and clicking it closes every other tab in the group instead of the one clicked. This
happens silently - nothing draws the user's attention to the fact that the icon
changed meaning between steps 2-3 and step 5, so the wrong action fires without any
warning.

## Suspected cause

`ModifierKeyEmitter` (`src/vs/base/browser/dom.ts`) resets `altKey` to `false` on the
window's `blur` event, which correctly clears the *modifier* state when focus leaves
VS Code. However, `MultiEditorTabsControl`'s `hoveredTabIndex`
(`src/vs/workbench/browser/parts/editor/multiEditorTabsControl.ts`) is only cleared by
a real `mouseleave` on the tab - not by the window losing focus. If the mouse doesn't
physically move during the Alt-Tab round trip, the tab stays "hovered", and the
Close→Close Others swap can be retriggered without any further mouse movement, purely
by however Alt's key state is (re)established when focus returns - which is not
always reliable across applications/window managers (this area already has known
workarounds for stale Alt state, e.g. #112347, #115810).

## Suggestion

Either clear `hoveredTabIndex` on window `blur` (mirroring the existing Alt-state
reset), or require the swapped "Close Others" state to be re-armed by a fresh
`keydown` on Alt received while VS Code has focus, rather than trusting
`modifierKeyEmitter.keyStatus.altKey` as a source of truth immediately after a focus
change.

title: Implement paste threshold adjustment and "Insert in Prompt" feature
body:
This pull request implements the proposed changes to improve the paste functionality in the chat input based on the feedback from issue #331852. The following key changes have been made:

- **Threshold Adjustment**: Increased the `pastedTextArtifactDefaultMinLength` from 1000 to 10000, and added a new minimum line requirement of 10. This change aims to reduce false positives for long URLs and dictated sentences that should remain inline.
  
- **Single Setting**: Introduced a new setting `chat.pasteAsAttachmentThreshold` in the Settings UI, which allows users to configure the paste threshold without the need for separate `auto` or `never` options.

- **"Insert in Prompt" Feature**: Added the ability to right-click on a pasted-text pill to replace its inline reference with the actual text, allowing users to drop the attachment easily. This feature has been implemented for both the main chat input and the Agents window.

- **Plain-text Paste Keybinding**: Bound the existing `editor.action.pasteAsText` command to `Ctrl+Shift+V` (or `Cmd+Shift+V` on Mac) when the chat input has focus, ensuring that plain text can be pasted without interference from chat providers.

- **Test Coverage**: Updated and added tests to ensure the new functionality works as intended, with all tests passing successfully.

The proposal to add a one-time inline hint for auto-attachments has been dropped based on feedback, as it was deemed unnecessary with the new threshold and insert feature. 

Please review the changes and provide feedback.

title: Hide the Changes pill for folderless chat sessions
body:
## Description

In a folderless (quick) chat, the session **Changes** pill rendered above the chat input but clicking it did nothing. `SinglePaneDockedTabsCoordinator._readTarget()` refuses a Changes tab when the session is a quick chat or has no workspace, so the editor the pill opened was reconciled away immediately. Single-pane is the default layout, and the pill's `when` clause explicitly allowed quick chats in that layout — so the pill was always inert there.

Rather than making the editor open for workspace-less sessions, the pill no longer shows at all when the session has no folder.

### Changes

- `changesActions.ts`: gate the `Menus.SessionHeaderMeta` contribution of `ViewAllChangesAction` on `SessionHasWorkspaceContext` instead of `or(IsQuickChatSessionContext.negate(), SinglePaneLayoutEnabledContext)`.

  ```ts
  when: ContextKeyExpr.and(
      SessionHasChangesContext,
      SessionHasWorkspaceContext
  )
  ```

  The old `or` term is subsumed: a quick chat never has a workspace (`QuickChatSessionKind.computeWorkspace` returns `undefined`, and workspace-less sessions are promoted to quick chat), and every non-quick-chat session already satisfied it. This also lines up with the sibling **Files** pill, which already requires `SessionHasWorkspaceContext`.

- `changesActions.test.ts` (new): evaluates the pill's `when` for three combinations — folderless + changes (hidden), workspace + changes (shown), workspace + no changes (hidden). Verified to fail against the previous clause.

### Note for reviewers

The in-response "N files changed +x −y" summary (`ChatTurnPillsContentPart`) is a separate workbench-level surface and is unchanged; it remains inert for folderless sessions. Happy to follow up if that one should be hidden too.

- Fixes #331967

title: Render the session changes pill from a cache
body:
The session changes pill only appeared once the provider reported its changes, which often arrives well after the session is opened — so the pill popped in late.

This remembers the changes pill last shown for each session and renders it optimistically the next time that session opens, so the pill is there immediately.

- New `ISessionChangesStatsCache` (`sessions/services/sessions/common/sessionChangesStatsCache.ts`), one entry per `sessionId`, persisted in global (`APPLICATION`) storage and shared across windows.
- Bounded at 30 entries; recording a session moves it to the newest position, and the oldest entry is evicted when a new one is added to a full cache.
- `readSessionChangesStats` is the single place that derives the pill counts from a session (provider `changesSummary`, else the default changeset, else the session changes), and distinguishes "not reported yet" from a reported "no changes".
- `ViewAllChangesActionViewItem` falls back to the cached counts while the session has not reported; the new `sessionHasCachedChanges` context key makes the pill visible in that window.
- A session that reports no changes drops its cached entry, so a stale pill is never kept around.

Covered by unit tests for the cache (LRU/eviction, persistence, dropping empty sessions) and for the optimistic context key.

title: Fix stale isActive causing background tabs to be reported as activeTab
body:
Fixes #331914

## Problem

`tabGroups.activeTabGroup.activeTab` can silently point at a background tab. Changing a background webview panel's `iconPath` or `title` — or its dirty, pin or preview state — flips the reported active tab to that background tab, even though the workbench keeps rendering and focusing the correct one.

## Root cause

`_onDidTabActiveChange` set `isActive = true` on the newly active tab's cached DTO but never cleared it on the tab that was active before:

```ts
const activeTab = tabs[editorIndex];
// No need to loop over as the exthost uses the most recently marked active tab
activeTab.isActive = true;
```

Skipping the loop is only safe while nothing re-sends one of those now-stale DTOs. But `_onDidTabLabelChange`, `_onDidTabDirty`, `_onDidTabPinChange` and `_onDidTabPreviewChange` all patch a single field and re-send the *whole* cached DTO — stale `isActive: true` included.

On the receiving side, `ExtHostEditorTabGroup.acceptTabOperation` trusts that flag and repoints `_activeTabId`, which backs both `TabGroup.activeTab` and `Tab.isActive`. Its `else if` guard only fires when the incoming DTO *is* the current active tab, so it cannot defend against a different tab arriving with a stale `true`.

Because the flag is never cleared, every tab visited during the session is a latent trigger.

## Fix

Clear `isActive` on the group's other tabs when the active tab changes, so no stale `true` survives in the cache. `activeTab.isActive = true` stays the first statement so an out-of-range `editorIndex` still throws before anything is mutated, letting the existing `catch` rebuild the model.

## Testing

Added a regression test to `mainThreadEditorTabs.test.ts` that drives a real `ExtHostEditorTabs` through a real `MainThreadEditorTabs` and asserts `activeTab` after each of the four update kinds.

Verified it fails without the fix — all four report `Panel A (2)` instead of `Panel B` — and passes with it. `npm run typecheck-client` is clean and the 18 `EditorTabs` unit tests pass.

title: fix(find): use textContent to reliably display matches count
body:
Fixes #316743

**Description of proposed changes:**
The Find Widget's matches count indicator occasionally failed to render its value due to issues with how the text node was being managed. Previously, the logic relied on `this._matchesCount.firstChild?.remove()` followed by an `appendChild(document.createTextNode(label))`. Depending on the runtime environment or specific DOM state anomalies, this teardown and recreation process could fail silently, leaving the matches count invisible to the user despite the widget otherwise functioning normally.

This PR refactors the match count update logic across the editor's Find Widgets (`findWidget.ts`, `notebookFindWidget.ts`, `simpleFindWidget.ts`) to use the standard `.textContent` API. This guarantees that the inner content is fully flushed and reliably replaced, preventing the label from disappearing and avoiding any node-tearing edge cases.

**How to test:**
1. Open any text file and press `Ctrl+F`.
2. Type a query that yields matches.
3. Verify that the matches count (e.g., "1 of 5") is correctly displayed in the Find Widget next to the navigation buttons.
4. Perform the same verification in a Notebook document and in the Terminal find widget.

title: Fix Disable button dropdown when extension is disabled globally (#244138)
body:
Fixes #244138
    
    ### Description
    Currently, when an extension is disabled globally but enabled for a specific workspace, the "Disable" button in the extensions view
  shows a dropdown containing both `"Disable"` and `"Disable (Workspace)"`. Since the extension is already disabled globally, the global
  `"Disable"` action should not be visible.

    This PR updates `DisableGloballyAction.update()` in `extensionsActions.ts` to verify if the extension is already globally disabled
  (`!this.extensionEnablementService.isDisabledGlobally(this.extension.local)`). By doing so, the global disable action is correctly
  hidden, resulting in a single "Disable (Workspace)" button without a dropdown, which is the expected behavior.

    ### How to test
    1. Install any extension and disable it globally.
    2. Enable the same extension for the current workspace.
    3. Open the Extensions view and click on the extension.
    4. Verify that the disable button is now simply "Disable (Workspace)" and no longer shows a dropdown with the global "Disable" option.

- VS Code Version: ms-vscode.powershell 2025.4.0
- OS Version:  Windows 11
- PowerShell Version:  5.1.26100.8875

Steps to Reproduce:

1. In VS Code, run with the "Play" button Connect-MgGraph

## Issue
The VS Code PowerShell Extension "Play" button fails to load `Microsoft.Graph.Authentication` v2.36.0–2.39.0 (works with v2.35.0).

## Description
When running a PowerShell script that uses the Microsoft Graph PowerShell SDK via the **Play** button in VS Code (using the `ms-vscode.powershell` extension), the following error occurs:

```text
Connect-MgGraph : The 'Connect-MgGraph' command was found in the module 'Microsoft.Graph.Authentication', but the module could not be loaded. For more information, run 'Import-Module Microsoft.Graph.Authentication'.
```

### Detailed Import Error
Manually importing the module inside the PowerShell Extension's current console produces this `TypeLoadException` error:

```text
Import-Module : Method 'GetTokenAsync' in type 'Microsoft.Graph.PowerShell.Authentication.Core.Utilities.UserProvidedTokenCredential' from assembly 'Microsoft.Graph.Authentication.Core, Version=2.39.0.0, 
Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=31bf3856ad364e35' does not have an implementation.
```

## Observations
* **Host Dependent:** The exact same script runs successfully in the classic PowerShell ISE, a standalone PowerShell console, and Azure Automation runbooks with `Microsoft.Graph.Authentication` 2.39.0.
* **Version Pinned:** The script functions perfectly in the VS Code PowerShell extension if `Microsoft.Graph.Authentication` is pinned strictly to version 2.35.0.
* **Scope:** The issue only triggers when using the Play button or working directly inside the VS Code PowerShell Extension terminal host across versions 2.36.0 through 2.39.0.

## Suspected Cause
The VS Code PowerShell extension relies on **PowerShell Editor Services (PSES)** for its runtime environment. The underlying issue appears to be an assembly conflict involving the `Azure.Core` or `Microsoft.Graph.Authentication.Core` DLLs. 

Newer versions of the Graph SDK introduce an updated or modified signature for `GetTokenAsync` in the `UserProvidedTokenCredential` class. Because PowerShell Editor Services pre-loads its own version of these dependencies into the shared session context, it prevents the Graph module from cleanly resolving its expected class implementation, resulting in a fatal `TypeLoadException`.

## Workaround
Downgrading and pinning the module to the last known working release resolves the issue:

```powershell
Install-Module Microsoft.Graph.Authentication -Force -RequiredVersion 2.35.0
```

title: Allow base URL override for OAIBYOKLMProvider
body: ### Problem Statement The built-in `OAIBYOKLMProvider` hardcodes its base URL to `https://api.openai.com/v1` (in `openAIProvider.ts`) and derives the final endpoints (such as `/responses` or `/chat/completions`) from that fixed base URL. This prevents users from using the built-in OpenAI provider with custom OpenAI-compatible endpoints, enterprise API proxies, or self-hosted/regional instances (e.g., Azure OpenAI) without falling back to a custom provider schema. ### Feature Request Allow overriding the base URL when using the standard `OAIBYOKLMProvider`. This would work similarly to configuring model providers in settings (**Model providers > Add provider / Configure Base URL**), enabling users to specify a custom base endpoint while retaining all standard `OAIBYOKLMProvider` behavior and capabilities.

VS Code Version: 1.132.1
OS Version: Sonoma 14.0 (23A344)

When I split a JSX/HTML tag into multiple lines, I expect the attributes to be vertically aligned with the first attribute (the one on the opening line). However, in VS Code, the indentation behaviour is inconsistent and does not follow the column of the first attribute.


Steps to Reproduce:

1. Start with a single‑line tag:

```tsx
<Space direction="row" size="s" align="center">
</Space>
```

2. Manually break the lines so that each attribute is on its own line, and the closing `>` is also on a new line:

```tsx
<Space direction="row" 
size="s" 
align="center"
>
</Space>
```

3. Run auto‑formatting – the attributes get indented, but not aligned with direction:

```tsx
<Space direction="row" 
    size="s" 
    align="center"
>
</Space>
```

4. Press `Tab` on each attribute line – they shift further right, but still not aligned with direction:

```tsx
<Space direction="row" 
        size="s" 
        align="center"
>
</Space>
```

5. To achieve the desired vertical alignment, I have to manually delete extra spaces until size and align start exactly under the `d` of `direction`:

```tsx
<Space direction="row" 
       size="s" 
       align="center"
>
</Space>
```

**Actual behaviour**

1. Neither auto‑formatting nor Tab respects the column of the first attribute (direction).
2. Indentation is based on a fixed level (e.g. one tab stop or a number of spaces), not on the position of the first attribute.
3. No built‑in command exists to align attributes vertically.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fa851de7-4689-4c44-a9cf-a8bcc9143387

**Expected behaviour**

1. When attributes are placed on separate lines, all attributes must start at the same column as the first attribute (i.e. vertically aligned under the d of direction).
2. Pressing Tab on any attribute line should align it to that column, or there should be a dedicated command/option to do so.

This is a standard behaviour in many IDEs (like IntelliJ IDEA) and saves a lot of manual formatting time. However, in VS Code, neither the built‑in formatter nor the `Tab` key respects the first attribute's column. Instead, they apply a fixed indentation level, which forces me to manually add/remove spaces every time.

Please consider adding a setting like `"editor.attributeAlignment": true` or a built‑in command to align attributes vertically. Additionally, make the `Tab` key smart enough to align to the first attribute's column.

I already filed a similar issue about auto-formatting, but this problem is deeper – no Tab correction, attribute alignment is no different from plain text. That's why I consider this a bug because writing code takes less time than formatting it.

Thank you.

body:
## Summary

Adds an initial Dev Container execution target for Agent Host sessions in the Agents window. Users can start a session from a local folder's existing Dev Container configuration and run the Agent Host inside the container.

Part of #317380.

<details>
<summary>Session Context</summary>

Key decisions from the development session:

- **Existing environment first**: This initial implementation reuses the selected folder's `.devcontainer/devcontainer.json` or `.devcontainer.json`, matching the primary user need to run agents with the project's existing tools and dependencies. It does not claim that arbitrary Dev Container configurations are hardened security sandboxes.
- **Local initial scope**: The checkbox is offered only for local file workspaces when Docker is available. Full composition with SSH, WSL, Dev Tunnels, and named-volume cloning remains future work.
- **Shared-process ownership**: Container creation, VS Code CLI installation, Agent Host startup, and the raw relay run in the shared process, parallel to the existing SSH architecture. The renderer owns the protocol client and dynamic Sessions provider.
- **Draft handoff**: The composer begins with a local draft because no container provider exists yet. On foreground Send, the draft immediately becomes In Progress while the container starts; once connected, it is replaced by an In Progress container-owned draft before `createNewChat`.
- **Failure behavior**: Preparation failures restore the original local draft to Untitled rather than leaving a stuck in-progress session.
- **CLI distribution**: VS Code bundles a pinned `@devcontainers/cli` and launches it through Electron-as-Node instead of relying on a separately installed CLI.
- **Output channels**: Dev Container CLI output is retained in one stable `Dev Container (<workspace>)` Output channel per source workspace, reused across connection attempts.
- **Control ordering**: `New Worktree` remains left of `Dev Container` across asynchronous availability and config rerenders.

</details>

## Changes

- Add the Dev Container checkbox to local Agent Host drafts when Docker and a supported config are present.
- Start or reuse the container with the bundled Dev Container CLI.
- Install/reuse the matching VS Code CLI and standalone Agent Host inside the container.
- Relay AHP over `devcontainer exec` through the shared process.
- Register a dynamic remote Agent Host provider for the container workspace.
- Transfer compatible config/model/mode state from the local draft to the container draft.
- Stream container setup output to a workspace-specific Output channel.
- Add lifecycle, availability, draft replacement, rollback, packaging, and UI-ordering coverage.

## Validation

- Client and build-tool typechecks
- Hygiene and layer validation
- Focused and full Sessions/Agent Host unit suites
- Live end-to-end validation against this repository's Dev Container, including a completed Agent Host turn from `/workspaces/vscode`

title: Agents - add isExternal and pull request fields to session telemetry
body:
Three related changes to Agents window telemetry.

### `isExternal` on every session-scoped event

`ISession.isExternal` tells us whether a session was discovered in an application other than the current host. It is now reported on all session-scoped events (`agents/requestSent`, the session action events, the feedback events, the sticky/maximize toggles) and on `agents/sessionSummary`.

The property is optional on `ISession` (absent means `false`), and provenance is only known once session metadata has loaded — which can happen after the summary tracking entry was created — so the persisted value is refreshed on every interaction rather than captured once.

### `pullRequestCount` and `pullRequestStatus` on the session summary

`agents/sessionSummary` now reports how many pull requests the session ended up with and the state of the most recent one: `open`, `closed`, `merged`, `draft`, or `undefined` when there is no PR or its state was never resolved.

The state is recovered from the icon on the session's GitHub info via a new `getPullRequestStatusFromIcon()`, added next to `computePullRequestIcon()` in `sessions/contrib/github/common/types.ts` so the two stay in sync. Like the change counts, both values are refreshed on every interaction, so the summary reports the last observed state. When GitHub info is absent (not yet resolved, or no GitHub repo) the last known values are kept rather than reset.

### `agents/requestSent` no longer counts the session it is reporting on

`_getAllSessionsFields` was handed the full session list, which includes the session the request was just sent to, so every bucket was inflated by one for the very session being reported on. `allWorkspacesNotDone` / `currentWorkspaceNotDone` always counted it, and the in-progress buckets counted it too once the provider had flipped its status — which it typically has, since `onDidSendRequest` fires after `provider.sendRequest` resolves. It also made the numbers inconsistent between a brand-new session (not yet in the list) and a follow-up.

The anchor session is now skipped. The comparison is by `sessionId` rather than object identity, because the send path fires the event with `updatedSession` — a fresh object the provider hands back — so an identity check would not have caught it. The comments on all twelve count fields now state that they exclude the session the request was sent to.

### Validation

`npm run typecheck-client` clean (this also verifies each event payload matches its classification) and eslint clean on the touched files.

New tests cover the external flag and its refresh, the PR count/status for a merged session with multiple PRs, a draft PR without a resolved main-PR icon, the zero/undefined case for a session with no GitHub info, and the anchor-session exclusion. The mock wiring in `sessionsTelemetry.contribution.test.ts` was extracted into a `setup(sessions)` helper, since the existing test inlined all twelve service mocks.

<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->

When an Agents window session is connected to a remote Agent Host Protocol (AHP) host, please allow integrated-browser traffic to be proxied through that session's remote host. This could be automatic for agent-opened tabs or an explicit per-tab **Browse through Agent Host** target.

## Why

The integrated browser can proxy through VS Code Remote workspace authorities, but a remote AHP host selected by an Agents window session is not treated as a proxy authority. As a result, an agent can run a service on its remote host but cannot open that service in the integrated browser without separately exposing or forwarding the port.

This also prevents secure loopback workflows where a browser needs to send an artifact directly to a one-use receiver on the selected agent host.

## Reproduction

Environment:

- Local client: VS Code 1.134.0 on macOS (integrated browser user agent: Electron 42.8.1 / Chrome 148)
- Remote AHP host: Windows, VS Code CLI/host 1.133.0
- Agents window session connected to that remote host
- Settings applied locally and the Agents window reloaded:

```json
"workbench.browser.enableRemoteProxy": true,
"workbench.browser.dataStorage": "workspace"
```

Steps:

1. On the remote Windows AHP host, start an HTTP server bound to `127.0.0.1:43127` that returns a unique nonce from `/probe`.
2. Verify from the remote host that `http://127.0.0.1:43127/probe` returns `200` and the nonce.
3. From the AHP-backed agent session, call the integrated-browser tool to open `http://127.0.0.1:43127/probe`.
4. Repeat with `http://localhost:43127/probe`.

Actual result:

- Both URLs fail with `net::ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED`.
- The request never reaches the remote Windows server.
- The browser tab shows no remote indicator.
- The URL is resolved against the local macOS client, not the AHP host.

Expected result:

- The selected remote AHP host is available as a browser proxy target.
- Agent-opened tabs associated with that session can reach HTTP/HTTPS endpoints visible only to the AHP host.
- The browser shows the remote indicator and preserves per-session isolation.

## Related, but not duplicates

- #293229 implemented proxying through Remote Workspace connections via `workbench.browser.enableRemoteProxy`.
- #321294 tested that feature for Tunnels, SSH, Dev Containers, WSL, and Codespaces, including agent-opened tabs.
- #314789 tracks broad embedded-browser parity for remote Agent Hosts in the Agents window, but does not describe routing localhost/browser traffic through the selected AHP host.
- #324828 concerned a Remote Workspace BrowserView regression; disabling remote proxy fixed that issue. Here, remote proxy never activates for the AHP host at all.

title: agentHost: isolate tool approval test workspace
body:
## Summary

Fixes the recurring macOS ARM Electron integration-test failure by running the Agent Host tool-approval containment tests against a small isolated temporary workspace instead of the full VS Code checkout.

## Root cause

The regression was introduced by [33e1911a](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/33e1911ac9cf64cf9f12f5c286808cc2f0882286) (`Refactor AgentService instantiation`). That change correctly replaced the nonexistent `file:///workspace` fixture with `URI.file(process.cwd())`, but this made each affected turn use the full VS Code repository as its working directory.

Before the scripted mock agent receives the message and emits `chat/toolCallStart`, the Agent Host awaits its turn-start checkpoint. For a real Git workspace this runs a full `git status --untracked-files=all` and captures the working tree through a temporary index. On the macOS ARM build agent, checkpointing the VS Code checkout takes about 6–6.25 seconds.

Protocol notification waits default to five seconds on non-Windows, so these tests timed out before the mock agent started:

- `auto-approves write to regular file (no pending confirmation)`
- `blocks write to .env file (requires manual confirmation)`

The related orphan-confirmation test used the same working directory but had an explicit eight-second notification timeout. It consistently passed in about six seconds, confirming that the failure was caused by fixture setup cost rather than permission behavior.

The failure first appeared in [build 466511](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=466511), after [build 466461](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=466461) passed, and reproduced with the same two timeouts in [build 466537](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=466537) and [build 466553](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=466553).

## Fix

- Create one temporary workspace for the permission integration suite.
- Pass its path to the standalone scripted mock through `VSCODE_AGENT_HOST_MOCK_WORKSPACE`.
- Resolve mock read/write permission paths against that workspace.
- Stop the Agent Host before removing the fixture.

This preserves the real path-containment behavior while avoiding a checkpoint over the full repository. It also keeps the mock's default `process.cwd()` behavior for other callers.

## Validation

- `npm run transpile-client`
- `npm run hygiene`
- `./scripts/test-integration.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/protocol/toolApproval.integrationTest.ts`
  - 7 passing in 790 ms
  - previously failing tests: 89 ms and 81 ms
  - orphan-confirmation test: 95 ms, down from approximately 6 seconds

title: Make remote browser proxy startup and first connection resilient
body:
## Summary

- represent the remote browser proxy as `stopped`, `starting`, `ready`, or `failed` instead of treating missing proxy information as both disabled and pending
- hold initial navigation until the local proxy is ready and Electron has applied it
- settle waiting navigation with a visible load error when local proxy startup fails, rather than leaving a blank tab forever
- retry one failed upstream tunnel handshake before any browser request bytes are sent, so an idle remote connection can wake without replaying the page navigation
- add regression coverage for pending, ready, failed, restart, direct-mode, HTTP recovery, CONNECT recovery, and bounded permanent failure

Related to #331909

## Safety

The upstream retry happens while establishing the transport, before request bytes are sent to the target. It therefore does not repeat an HTTP request, change the browser URL, or create another tab. A second connection failure remains terminal.

## Testing

- `npm run transpile-client`
- `npm run eslint -- <15 touched files>`
- `npm run typecheck-client`

The acceptance test will disable the extension's navigation retries, leave the Tunnel idle for at least 60 seconds, and require the first unchanged URL to render without a reload or manual retry. title: Perf: Register built-in notebook types declaratively
body:
## Summary

Register the Interactive Window notebook type declaratively instead of instantiating `INotebookService` during workbench restoration.

- Add a lightweight registry for built-in notebook type metadata.
- Register the Interactive notebook type at module load alongside its editor pane.
- Merge built-in types when `NotebookProviderInfoStore` is first materialized.
- Preserve built-in metadata over stale entries restored from the notebook-type memento.
- Keep Interactive editor resolver registration in `BlockRestore`.

## Startup scenario impact

The standard startup scenario restores one text editor and does not open an Interactive Window. Previously, `InteractiveDocumentContribution` still injected `INotebookService` and called `getContributedNotebookType('interactive')`.

That query materialized `NotebookProviderInfoStore`, which transitively initialized notebook, editor resolver, configuration, storage, file, and accessibility dependencies during blocking workbench restoration.

With this change, ordinary startup registers only lightweight editor resolver metadata. The Interactive notebook type remains globally declared, but its provider object and dependencies are materialized only when notebook provider information is actually needed.

## Measurements

Both variants were independently minified from the same source commit and overlaid onto the same Insiders runtime. The startup scenario restored one text editor in a deterministic folder with extensions and GPU acceleration disabled.

### Uninstrumented warm startup

30 per-start alternating pairs:

| Metric | Baseline | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Median total startup | 1406 ms | 1398 ms |
| Median paired difference |  | **-7 ms** |
| Bootstrap 95% interval |  | **-14 ms to -1.5 ms** |

Critical phase markers:

| Marker | Paired difference | 95% interval |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Renderer startup | **-9 ms** | -12 ms to -3.5 ms |
| Workbench startup | **-5 ms** | -8 ms to -1 ms |
| Blocking contribution creation | **-2 ms** | -2 ms to -1 ms |

### Profiled renderer startup

Three measured warmed traces:

| Metric | Baseline | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `didStartRenderer` to `didStartWorkbench` | 1502.2 ms | 1475.5 ms (**-26.7 ms**) |
| `workbench.contrib.interactiveDocument` | 3.1-3.3 ms | **0.2-0.3 ms** |

Trace instrumentation increases absolute startup time, but all three traces show that the Interactive contribution no longer pulls the notebook provider initialization chain onto the startup critical path.

## Architecture and compatibility

- `InteractiveEditorInput` does not own global registration or reference-counting state.
- The built-in type registry follows VS Code's platform `Registry` pattern.
- Registrations return disposables, allowing tests and future non-process-lifetime consumers to clean up.
- The provider store owns the materialized provider entries and disposes them with its existing lifecycle.
- Interactive editor resolver registration remains blocking, so opening and restoring Interactive Windows continues to work.
- Existing cached notebook type metadata cannot conflict with the declarative built-in entry.

## Validation

- Full client compile and type-check
- Targeted ESLint
- Notebook provider registry unit tests
- Minified production bundle
- Interactive Window real-UI scenario:
  - Open an Interactive Window
  - Close it
  - Reopen it successfully
- Three paired startup traces
- 30 paired uninstrumented warm startup runs

title: Integrated Browser intermittently drops initial localhost navigation in Remote Tunnel after idle

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issue identified by VS Code Team member as probable bug

labels.name: browser-integration
labels.description: Web browsing features integrated into VS Code (e.g. integrated browser)

body:
## Environment

- VS Code 1.132.1 (`c2d1b13fdc4a77628e5f3bb70173351c8f2fbad1`)
- Desktop connected to a Linux host through Remote Tunnel
- Desktop client OS is macOS (26.2); the remote host is Linux
- `workbench.browser.enableRemoteProxy: true`
- HTTP server listening only on remote `localhost`

## Reproduction

1. On the remote host, start a server that logs every request:

   ```sh
   node -e "require('http').createServer((req,res)=>{console.log(Date.now(),req.url);res.end('ok')}).listen(8123,'localhost')"
   ```

2. From a Remote Tunnel extension, open one fixed URL in the Integrated
   Browser:

   ```js
   await vscode.commands.executeCommand('workbench.action.browser.open', {
     url: 'http://localhost:8123/repro/fixed',
     openToSide: false,
     reuseUrlFilter: '/repro/**'
   });
   ```

3. Leave new-tab navigation idle for about 60 seconds.
4. Repeat the command. If the tab stays blank, repeat the same command with the
   byte-identical URL every ~1.5 seconds.

## Expected

The initial navigation waits for the remote browser connection and reaches the
remote server once.

## Actual

The tab opens, but the initial navigation can produce no server request and is
never replayed. Reissuing the identical URL eventually succeeds.

In one measured Remote Tunnel run after 56 seconds idle:

- the tab opened at `21:46:41.826` UTC;
- the remote backend remained reachable from the remote extension host in
  9–14 ms;
- the initial navigation plus two identical re-navigations produced no server
  request;
- the fourth identical navigation reached the server at `21:46:46.845`, 5.02 s
  after the initial command;
- the page rendered at `21:46:47.581`, 5.76 s after the initial command.

A separate run with retries disabled remained blank for 40 seconds with no
server request. Waiting alone therefore did not recover the navigation.

## Diagnostics / likely readiness gap

The current readiness promise covers applying Electron's local proxy
configuration, but the upstream remote connection is established later and
lazily. Proxy intent can also be enabled while proxy information is still
absent, with `undefined` representing both “off” and “not ready.” A transient
upstream failure resets the HTTP response and does not replay the navigation.

Relevant source:

- [`BrowserSessionRemote.whenReady`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/c2d1b13fdc4a77628e5f3bb70173351c8f2fbad1/src/vs/platform/browserView/electron-main/browserSessionRemote.ts#L95-L138)
- [`BrowserView.loadURL`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/c2d1b13fdc4a77628e5f3bb70173351c8f2fbad1/src/vs/platform/browserView/electron-main/browserView.ts#L689-L694)
- [Lazy upstream connection and reset-on-error](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/c2d1b13fdc4a77628e5f3bb70173351c8f2fbad1/src/vs/platform/tunnel/node/tunnelProxy.ts#L364-L407)

## Candidate fix and tests

Represent remote proxy state as `off | pending | ready | failed`, and hold the
initial navigation while proxying is pending. Include the upstream remote
connection in readiness, or replay the initial idempotent navigation once
after a transient wake/reconnect failure. Surface a bounded error rather than
leaving a blank tab.

Add regression tests that delay both proxy-info delivery and the upstream
tunnel connection, then assert the initial URL reaches the server exactly once
after readiness. Add a transient first-connect failure case and assert
automatic recovery without another user navigation.

## Related, not duplicate

- [#321294 — Browser in Remote Workspaces test plan](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/321294): Tunnel coverage, but no idle/reconnect case.
- [#324828 — localhost request fails before reaching backend](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/324828): similar symptom, but Dev Container/custom `.localhost` hostname and persistent behavior.
- [#321440 — managed connection proxy support](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/321440): earlier managed-connection problem, already fixed.

Desktop-side **Extension Host** output around a failed attempt can be provided
in a follow-up if needed; that is where the proxy runs.

title: Dispose AgentHostPty on terminal shutdown, exit, and detach
body:
Resolves: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/331889

- Dispose the client-side `AgentHostPty` after `shutdown()` and after a host-originated `TerminalExited` action, deferring the exit event one microtask because `TerminalProcessManager` calls `shutdown()` while its exit listener is still attached.
- Use one lifetime `CancellationTokenSource` and one replaceable subscription generation so pending startup and reconnect hydration settle on shutdown or replacement; the hydration wait is built from `DeferredPromise`, `disposableTimeout`, and `raceCancellation`.
- Keep host ownership explicit: client-owned terminals request server cleanup immediately and again once an in-flight `createTerminal` settles; attach-only tool terminals finalize locally without deleting the host terminal.
- Release the host terminal when a reconnect fails before the PTY ever signaled ready, matching the `shutdown()` pairing; a terminal that was already ready stays untouched when reconnect fails.
- Add a terminal-instance-owned registration backstop for paths that clear the process reference before instance disposal (Detach Session); a PTY created after its instance was disposed is disposed locally without sending `disposeTerminal`, and a stale revived registration cannot overwrite or remove a replacement.
- Log through `ITerminalLogService`, injected by `AgentHostTerminalService` and passed to `AgentHostPty` as a plain constructor parameter.
- Cover shutdown, natural exit, duplicate finalization, pending creation and hydration, reconnect replacement and timeout, stale-timeout inertness, attach-only ownership, instance disposal, late factories, and creation failures with behavioral tests (faked timers for the 10s hydration timeout, no monkey-patched `dispose`).

-----------------------------------------
Inspirations from:

- Self-disposal after forwarding process exit follows [`TerminalProcessExtHostProxy.emitExit`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/07c20d96cf3f2cbc8142ac7079ba9048cf7f6134/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/browser/terminalProcessExtHostProxy.ts#L86-L89).
- The distinction between client shutdown and process-originated exit follows [`TerminalProcessManager.dispose`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/07c20d96cf3f2cbc8142ac7079ba9048cf7f6134/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/browser/terminalProcessManager.ts#L208-L222) and [`TerminalProcessManager._onExit`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/07c20d96cf3f2cbc8142ac7079ba9048cf7f6134/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/browser/terminalProcessManager.ts#L700-L715).
- The one-microtask exit deferral accounts for `shutdown()` running while the manager's exit listener is still attached, in [`TerminalProcessManager.dispose`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/07c20d96cf3f2cbc8142ac7079ba9048cf7f6134/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/browser/terminalProcessManager.ts#L208-L222) and [`SeamlessRelaunchDataFilter.newProcess`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/07c20d96cf3f2cbc8142ac7079ba9048cf7f6134/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/browser/terminalProcessManager.ts#L796-L798).
- The instance-owned backstop accounts for the detach ordering in [`TerminalProcessManager.detachFromProcess`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/07c20d96cf3f2cbc8142ac7079ba9048cf7f6134/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/browser/terminalProcessManager.ts#L237-L240) and [`TerminalInstance.detachProcessAndDispose`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/07c20d96cf3f2cbc8142ac7079ba9048cf7f6134/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/browser/terminalInstance.ts#L1366-L1371); registering it on `instance.store` relies on `onDisposed` firing after `processManager.dispose()` and before the store is disposed in [`TerminalInstance.dispose`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/07c20d96cf3f2cbc8142ac7079ba9048cf7f6134/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/browser/terminalInstance.ts#L1354-L1361).
- `ITerminalLogService` usage in a pty follows [`RemotePty`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/07c20d96cf3f2cbc8142ac7079ba9048cf7f6134/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/browser/remotePty.ts#L21); passing it as a required plain constructor parameter on a non-DI class follows [`BaseTerminalBackend`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/07c20d96cf3f2cbc8142ac7079ba9048cf7f6134/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/browser/baseTerminalBackend.ts#L32-L34).
- The hydration wait reuses [`DeferredPromise`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/07c20d96cf3f2cbc8142ac7079ba9048cf7f6134/src/vs/base/common/async.ts#L1827) and [`disposableTimeout`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/07c20d96cf3f2cbc8142ac7079ba9048cf7f6134/src/vs/base/common/async.ts#L612).
- The branded `NullLogService` test double is copied semantically from [`createLogService`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/07c20d96cf3f2cbc8142ac7079ba9048cf7f6134/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminalContrib/chatAgentTools/test/browser/basicExecuteStrategy.test.ts#L18-L20).

title: Renderer and NodeService memory growth causes repeated Linux OOM kills and V8 OOM crash (code 132) during long Copilot Agent sessions
body:
### Additional data point

This appears closely related to #315630 and #311225. The problem is still reproducible on VS Code 1.134.0.

Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: **Unknown**. The failure is intermittent and generally takes several hours. GitHub Copilot is bundled with this VS Code build.

### Environment

- VS Code: 1.134.0
- Commit: 110a328ea54b42367b803ec53ee0bf52ef26b419
- Package: 1.134.0-1787078834, amd64
- Electron: 42.8.1
- Chromium: 148.0.7778.280
- Node.js: 24.18.1
- V8: 14.8.178.38-electron.0
- Bundled GitHub Copilot: 0.62.0
- OS: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS, x86_64
- Kernel: 6.17.0-1022-azure
- Desktop/session: XFCE, X11 via xrdp
- CPU: 4 vCPU, Intel Xeon Platinum 8370C
- Memory: 15 GiB, no swap
- Installed extensions: 99

### Usage pattern

1. Open multiple local VS Code windows containing large Python/TypeScript workspaces.
2. Use Copilot Agent for tool-heavy, long-running sessions.
3. Keep the windows open for several hours.
4. Renderer memory grows until the kernel kills the process or V8 terminates it.

The exact action that triggers the final allocation failure is not yet known.

### Crash evidence

`main.log` shows four renderer losses in one session:

~~~text
2026-08-20 16:59:47.877 [error] CodeWindow: renderer process gone (reason: killed, code: 9)
2026-08-20 17:03:11.206 [error] CodeWindow: renderer process gone (reason: killed, code: 9)
2026-08-20 21:57:21.059 [error] CodeWindow: renderer process gone (reason: killed, code: 9)
2026-08-21 04:22:24.800 [error] CodeWindow: renderer process gone (reason: crashed, code: 132)
~~~

The first three events match Linux kernel OOM-killer records:

~~~text
Out of memory: Killed process 640503 (code), anon-rss: 4365680 kB
Out of memory: Killed process 655846 (code), anon-rss: 3995044 kB
Out of memory: Killed process 639699 (code), anon-rss: 4081976 kB
~~~

The code-132 crash matches a kernel native trap:

~~~text
2026-08-21 04:22:23 kernel: traps: code[676025] trap invalid opcode ... in code
~~~

Crashpad completed report `5270b517-eafe-4eb5-9d82-24339c7a0a8b` identifies the crashed process as `renderer` and contains V8 OOM data:

~~~text
heap.used: 1617648408
Heap: used=1542.7MB limit=4096.0MB
Mark-Compact (reduce) 1542.7 -> 1542.7 MB
current mu = 0.000
allocation failure; GC in old space requested
~~~

A second completed report, `7cd6127b-844d-4df7-b025-db7505eb97b4`, was generated on 2026-08-19. It identifies `node.mojom.NodeService` as the failed utility process:

~~~text
heap.used: 3501854508
electron.v8-oom.location: CALL_AND_RETRY_LAST
Mark-Compact (reduce) 3339.6 -> 3339.6 MB
current mu = 0.000
~~~

After the renderer crash, the extension host reports that the renderer closed its MessagePort and then exits normally with code 0. This suggests the extension-host shutdown is a consequence rather than the initial crash.

A current post-crash snapshot shows 44 VS Code processes using approximately 12.91 GiB aggregate RSS on a 15 GiB machine.

### Expected behavior

Renderer, Copilot Agent, and utility-process memory should remain bounded. Long-running sessions should not exhaust system memory or terminate workspace windows.

### Crash dumps

Both minidumps are retained locally and can be provided privately to maintainers. I am not attaching them publicly because they contain recoverable Copilot session content and local filesystem paths.

title: agentHost: fix legacy Copilot CLI migration issues (opening, worktrees, archived state)
body:
Follow-up to #331606, which migrates a legacy extension-host Copilot CLI session into the agent host when the user opens it. Migration succeeded on disk, but the session could then disappear from every list, silently reopen as legacy, or come
back unarchived.

Behind `chat.agentSessions.migrateLegacyCopilotCli` (experimental, default off). Sessions are untouched when it is disabled.

**Opening a migrated session no longer opens the legacy one.** Migration finishes just before the session is opened, so the migrated session had not always reached the sessions list yet. Opening then fell back to the legacy session it had just replaced — migration looked like it had done nothing, and the next open migrated it again.

**Worktree sessions now migrate correctly.** A worktree-isolated session was filtered out of the window opened on its own repository, so migrating it appeared to do nothing. A deleted worktree is also recreated on resume instead of failing, matching how native worktree sessions already behave.

**Sessions are no longer lost.** Migration claims the chat on disk, which is what makes the extension host stop listing it. If any later step failed, the session existed in no list at all. Sessions that cannot be migrated now stay on the legacy provider, and one that fails to restore reports an error like any other session.

**Archived state is preserved,** so migrating no longer resurfaces sessions the user had filed away.

**Diagnosability.** Adoption records why it did or did not migrate a session, in both logs and telemetry, so a migration that did nothing can be diagnosed from an agent host log instead of reproduced.

title: sessions: Centre the chat pill chevron on the compact glyph
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #331794, which landed the chat pill path/URI hovers and centred the dropdown chevron with a `transform: translateY(1px)` nudge on `chevron-down`.

- **Use `chevron-down-compact` for the pill's dropdown affordance.** `chevron-down` is drawn above the middle of the pill's 12px glyph slot, so it needed a hard-coded 1px nudge to reach the label's optical centre. `chevron-down-compact` is drawn on the box centre and lands on the label with no transform. It is also the glyph the workspace picker, session type picker and automation dialog dropdown triggers already use, so the sessions window now has one dropdown chevron.
- **Drop the `[class*='codicon-']` substring matchers** on the pill's two glyph rules. Per `css-best-practices.instructions.md` a single substring class matcher defeats Blink's per-class invalidation; both rules already win on specificity without it.
- **Share the artifact location helper with the pill debug overlay** instead of rebuilding the same hover, aria description and tooltip values there.

## Measurement

Rendered the pill with the production cascade (`.monaco-text-button.small` label at 11px/14px, glyph slot at `--vscode-codiconFontSize-compact`) and compared the chevron's ink centre against the label's ink centre:

| chevron | offset from label centre |
| --- | --- |
| `chevron-down`, no transform | **-1.06px** (visibly high) |
| `chevron-down` + `translateY(1px)` | -0.06px |

## Summary

Defer the four contributions that populate dynamic language-model setting enums until after the workbench has restored:

- Explore agent default model

- Utility model
- Utility small model

These contributions update Settings schema metadata. Runtime model resolution reads the configured value independently and does not depend on these arrays being populated during startup.

## Background

An overall profile-driven audit of the latest Insiders startup found `workbench.contrib.exploreAgentDefaultModel` taking approximately 3.5 ms during `BlockRestore`. The other three related contributions were individually small because the first contribution paid the cost of initializing shared language-model and configuration/schema infrastructure.

The initial arrays already contain the valid default/automatic option. Each contribution continues to:

- Populate the available model IDs, labels, and descriptions.
- Subscribe to language-model registration changes.
- Notify the configuration registry when the dynamic schema changes.

The only change is that this setup occurs in `AfterRestored` rather than blocking editor and workbench restoration.

## Measurements

Both variants were independently minified from the same source commit and overlaid onto the same Insiders runtime. The startup scenario restored one text editor in a deterministic folder with extensions and GPU acceleration disabled.

title: Add end-to-end trace logging for opening a session
body:
Opening a session runs through a long chain — the sessions list, the chat model load, an AHP round trip, the agent host''s session restore and its SQLite reads, the turn→history conversion, and finally the chat widget render. Most of that chain had no logging, so it was not possible to tell from a log file how long opening a session took or where the time went.

This adds `trace` markers along that whole path. Log lines are already timestamped, so no stopwatch code was added; each marker carries the session resource so one open can be followed end to end.

### Covered path

Both list entry points are covered:

- **Agents window** (`src/vs/sessions`): `SessionsService.openSession` → `ChatView.setChat`
- **Workbench chat sessions list**: `openSession` in `agentSessionsOpener.ts`

They funnel into the shared path:

`ChatService.loadRemoteSession` → `ChatSessionsService.getOrCreateChatSession` → `AgentHostSessionHandler.provideChatSessionContent` → AHP `subscribe` → `AgentService.subscribe` / `restoreSession` / `_restoreSessionState` / `_getChatMessages` → provider event read → back to the client's history→model conversion → `ChatWidget` first render.

### Notes

- Markers were added **only where none existed**. `ChatWidgetService.openSession` and `ChatViewPane.loadSession` were already instrumented and are untouched.
- `AgentService.subscribe` now reports whether the snapshot was served from memory or required a restore, which is the single biggest branch in the backend cost.
- `ChatWidget` logs the first render for a newly bound model once, tracked by session resource so a render triggered while the outgoing model unbinds cannot be misattributed and rapid switching cannot log the wrong session.
- The one non-log change is in `AgentService._getChatMessages`, where a nested `await` was split into two statements so the provider read can be bracketed; evaluation order is unchanged.

### Validation

- `tsc --project ./src/tsconfig.json --noEmit`
- `build/hygiene.ts` over the changed files
- `eslint` over the changed files

body:
Closing an Agent Host terminal disposes the server-side shell, but the client-side `AgentHostPty` can remain undisposed.

I saw this while testing Agents Window terminal cleanup:

```text
[LEAKED DISPOSABLE] Error: CREATED via:
    at new BasePty
    at new AgentHostPty
    at Object.customPtyImplementation
    at TerminalProcessManager.createProcess
```

`AgentHostPty.shutdown()` clears the subscription and emits process exit, but does not dispose the `AgentHostPty` object itself. Shutdown can also remain blocked if initial subscription hydration never completes.

Steps to reproduce:

1. Create an Agent Host terminal.
2. Close/dispose the terminal.
3. Watch the development disposable tracker output.

The server-side terminal should be disposed and the client-side `AgentHostPty` lifecycle should complete without a leaked-disposable warning. This should also handle shutdown while initial subscription hydration is still pending.

title: Fix chat math ResizeObserver loop warnings
body:
## Summary

Fixes the concentrated `ChatMarkdownContentPart.mathLayout` ResizeObserver warning by removing redundant nested observation and folding math scrollbar convergence into the existing chat row observer.

## Root cause

Late KaTeX font metric changes resize both the markdown content and its containing virtualized row. The nested math observer participates in the same delivery cycle as `ChatListItemRenderer.itemHeight`, producing skipped notifications:

```text
ResizeObserverLoopContext(
  ChatListItemRenderer.itemHeight,
  ChatMarkdownContentPart.mathLayout
)
```

Making the math observer callback a no-op still reproduced the warning, proving that `scanDomNode()` writes were not the cause. Removing the redundant nested observer eliminated it.

## Fix

- Math markdown parts register their scrollbar layout callbacks with the owning row.
- The existing row observer runs those callbacks synchronously before publishing the final row height.
- Registrations follow each markdown part's render lifecycle, including nested markdown in tool and confirmation parts.
- No animation-frame deferral or production timing change is introduced.

## Validation

- Real KaTeX/CSS Chromium fixture: 7 native warnings before, 0 after.
- Math overflow remains horizontally scrollable after asynchronous font metric changes.
- Existing chat ResizeObserver scenarios remain warning-free.
- Native warning positive control still emits and preserves observer context.
- `compile-client`
- 26 `ChatMarkdownContentPart` unit tests
- 6 targeted Playwright tests

Fixes #316501

title: Dispose Agents Window terminals when sessions are archived
body:
Resolves: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/329316
Follow-up: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/331884
Follow-up: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/331889

- Dispose terminal instances owned by an Agents Window session when it transitions to archived instead of moving them to the background.
- Keep the existing one-time archive transition guard so provider re-emits do not affect terminals opened later.
- Close an untracked restored terminal only when it is persistent, inactive, and exactly matches a local archived worktree that no other live session shares.
- Preserve repository terminals, remote terminals, manually created terminals, standalone terminals, hidden tool terminals, and terminals owned by another session.
- Delay default-cwd assignment and terminal creation while the session is loading, archived, or waiting for its worktree.
- Invalidate asynchronous terminal creation and archive cleanup across archive, restore, and worktree-readiness generations.
- Recreate the active session terminal when restore happens during a late close confirmation, and keep ownership when the user cancels terminal disposal.
- Keep generic terminal visibility and AgentHostPty shutdown lifecycle out of scope; track those separately in #331884 and #331889.
- Add focused regression coverage for archive re-emits, shared worktrees/cwds, restored terminals, close vetoes, in-flight creation, rapid restore, worktree readiness, remote path safety, hidden tool terminals, and fresh terminal creation after restore.

-----------------------------------------
Inspirations from:

- The one-time archive transition guard comes from [SessionsTerminalContribution archive tracking](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/c21b01c8db3136bf20f0e45baf3eb4b32baeab8c/src/vs/sessions/contrib/terminal/browser/sessionsTerminalContribution.ts#L226-L260).
- Exact terminal ownership comes from the existing [session ID to terminal instance tracking](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/c21b01c8db3136bf20f0e45baf3eb4b32baeab8c/src/vs/sessions/contrib/terminal/browser/sessionsTerminalContribution.ts#L417-L428).
- Terminal close confirmation and disposal semantics come from [TerminalService.safeDisposeTerminal](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/c21b01c8db3136bf20f0e45baf3eb4b32baeab8c/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/browser/terminalService.ts#L430-L443).
